title: 1985 AHSME Problem 3
statement: In right \(\triangle ABC\) with legs \(5\) and \(12,\) arcs of circles are drawn, one with center \(A\) and radius \(12,\) the other with center \(B\) and radius \(5.\) They intersect the hypotenuse in \(M\) and \(N.\) Then \(MN\) has length

solutions.text:
The hypotenuse has length \(13.\) Since \(AM=12,\) point \(M\) is \(12\) units from \(A.\) Also \(BN=5,\) so \(AN=AB-BN=13-5=8.\) Therefore \(MN=AM-AN\) \(=12-8=4.\)

Thus the correct answer is D.
hints: First find the hypotenuse of the \(5\)-\(12\)-right triangle
Measure the positions of both arc intersections from \(A\)
